title: Concentric Circles
caption: Star trails over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Bright star trails fill the sky over ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile, curving into near-perfect concentric arcs and circles. At the center of the frame stands the retired Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope, while the ESO 3.6-meter telescope crowns the mountain on the left, glowing with activity.

The trails come from Earth turning on its axis. As the planet rotates, the stars seem to drift across the sky, slowly drawing those rings. Recording them takes a long exposure, so a photograph like this is really a record of time passing.

HARPS, the High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher, is installed on the 3.6-meter telescope. It hunts for exoplanets by measuring the tiny wobble of a star as an unseen planet circles it, tugging the star back and forth over each orbit.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure star-trail photograph credited to ESO/B. Tafreshi. The source does not publish camera or color-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. The rings appear only because the long exposure recorded the sky turning.
